arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the side that brought the case's counsel argued the Court never applied laches to federal limitations periods.
the opposing side's counsel argued the lower courts correctly applied laches to bar the suit.
The Solicitor General argued the 1957 amendment did not abrogate laches.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute centers on whether the equitable doctrine of laches can dismiss a copyright infringement suit filed within the statutory deadline. the side that brought the case contends the statute of limitations controls. the opposing side argues laches independently bars the claim.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case determines whether copyright holders can delay filing suit indefinitely. It defines the boundary between statutory deadlines and equitable defenses. It affects how courts handle stale copyright claims.
